0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Iridian Standards Institution on 18 September 1969, after the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilseeds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council and tl.e Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Niger seed plant grows to some extent in manv States in India and has attained considerable importance as an oils~{'d crop in Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Orissa and Maharashtra. The niger seed is also known indigenously as RA1\1TIL and SURGIYA. The oil derived from the seeds is used principally for edible purposes.
0.3 The oil obtained from niger seeds is covered in IS: 3490-1965*.

0.4 This standard contains clause 5.1 which calls for agreement between the purchaser and the supplier.
0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a parricular requirement of this standard is complied with, the fi.nal value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded oil' in accordance with. IS: 2-l960t. The number of significant places retained in the rounded otf value should be the same as that of the specified v.rlue in this standard.
1. SCOPE

1.1 This standard prescribes the methods of grading and rcqu ircnu-nts for the niger seeds for oil milling, along with the relevant methods of sampling and test. 2. TERMINOLOGY

2.1 For the pllrpose of this standard definitions given under :2 1966::: shall apply. .

IS: 5293.1969 3. GRADES

3.1 The material shall be of two grades, namely, Grade I and Grade 2.
4. REQUIREMENTS

4.1 The material shall be derived from the plant Guizotia abyssynica Cass., fam. Compositae. 4.2 The material shall be clean and free from foreign matter, dirt and oilseeds other than niger seeds.
4.3 The seeds shall not emit any foul odour or found deformed due to moist conditions.

4.4 The niger seeds shall also be free from non-edible seeds, such as MAHUA, castor, NEEloJ and argeu.one.
4.5 The material shall also comply with the requirements given in Table I.

5. PACKING 5.1 The material shall be supplied packed in clean, dry, sound, single, new or unmended hessian bags in merchantable condition as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 6. MARKING 6.1 The bags shall be marked with the name, grade and weight of the material in the bag; and the year of the crop and the source of supply. 7. SAMPLING 7.1 Representative samples of the material shall be drawn as prescribed in 18:4115-1967*.
8. TES1'S

8.1 Tests shall be carried out as prescribed in IS: 3579-1966t. 8.2 Quality of RellgeDts - Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water (see IS: 1070-1960t ) shall be usedin the tests.
NOTE - 'Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis.
